messages:
incident-bot: Pager: multiple GPU OOMs observed during prefill on us-west-2-prod serving cluster. Severity: P2. Runbook: prefill-oom. Notifying oncall.
ben (oncall): I'm on it — assigning to eng-runtime + infra. tagging folks.
maya: hitting container restarts on gpu-pool-3, nodes node-37 and node-42. Crash loop starts during large-context prefill (>100k tokens).
alex: logs show OOM during allocate for KV cache; example from pod gpu-svc-7f4d: 
```
2026-03-17T02:12:03Z ERROR runtime: Allocation failed: CUDA out of memory
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
container exited with code 137
```
maya: customer impact: ~2.8% of requests fail with 502/stream resets, concentrated on fin-analytics-prod model-route. Customers with long prompts see degraded responses.
ben (oncall): tagging @tina-sre for mitigation steps. Please confirm whether to throttle or evict.
tina: oncall-sre here — immediate plan: 1) apply soft-prefill cap at router (max_prefill_tokens=65536) 2) route long requests to smaller-model pool (ggml-7b -> 3b fallback) 3) cordon node-42 for live investigation.
infra-bot: Applied taint: kubectl taint nodes node-42 emergency=true:NoSchedule — pods will be drained.
ben (oncall): executing rollout: kubectl cordon node-42; kubectl drain node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data; scaling up fallback pool to handle spike.
alex: i ran `kubectl logs -n prod gpu-svc-7f4d -c runtime | tail -n 60` — seeing repeated allocator warnings and fragmentation traces. nvml shows free memory but alloc fails. Likely GPU memory fragmentation plus huge KV allocations.
maya: reproducer: send a 130k-token prefill to route; runtime tries to allocate KV ~1.5GB chunks and fails intermittently.
tina: immediate mitigation pushed: router config updated -> `prefill_token_hard_limit: 65536`, `prefill_trim: true` (trim oldest tokens when possible). Also enabled model-variant-fallback for route fin-analytics-prod.
ben (oncall): notified customer ops. cust-success please prepare customer-facing note.
cust-success: drafting message: "We observed transient GPU OOMs affecting long-context requests. We've applied protective limits and rerouted long requests to a smaller model. No data loss; degraded responses possible for very long prompts. We'll follow up with timeline and postmortem."
infra-bot: Node diagnostics snapshot for node-37: `nvidia-smi` output attached — memory shows small free segments; dmesg contains repeated `Out of memory` kernel kills for process 2345.
alex: plan for follow-up: (A) add allocator-level guard to refuse prefill allocations above X when fragmentation detected, (B) add per-request prefill token metering and reject with 413 if over hard limit, (C) improve cold-model fallback path to avoid container restarts.
tina: rolling restart completed for node-42; node-37 is in maintenance for deeper kernel + driver logs. No further restarts after throttles applied.
ben (oncall): customer impact estimate: ~300 requests failed over 40 minutes, primarily for 2 enterprise customers. Ops updated them at 02:45 UTC.
maya: filed follow-up ticket INC-4723 to add prefill-aware autoscaling and better error codes for clients when prefill denied.
alex: also putting together an infra changelist: increase fragmentation resilience in allocator and expose runtime metric `prefill_alloc_failures`.
cust-success: customer A acknowledged mitigation and accepted workaround (shorten prompt or use streaming prefix trim). Customer B requested timeline for permanent fix.
ben (oncall): closing live mitigation loop — safeguards remain in place. creating postmortem and linking runbook updates. Marking incident as mitigated.
incident-bot: Incident update: mitigated at 2026-03-17T02:17:40Z. Follow-up: postmortem + runbook update assigned to eng-runtime.
